title: Standard nearby-cycle constructibility and vanishing for a constructible sheaf on the generic fibre
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring: a henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal nonzero maximal ideal and separably closed residue field $k$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, choose a separable closure $\bar\eta$ of $\eta$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $S$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $i:X_k\to X$ and $\bar j:X_{\bar\eta}\to X$ for the fibre maps, and $\pi:X_{\bar\eta}\to X_\eta$ for the projection to the generic fibre. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $R$ and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by $\ell^n$ for some $n\geq1$. For every constructible etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ on the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], the sheaf $i^*R^q\bar j_*(\pi^*F)$ is constructible on $X_k$ for every integer $q\geq0$, and $i^*R^q\bar j_*(\pi^*F)=0$ for all sufficiently large $q$. Here inverse image and derived direct image are [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No finite Tor assumption on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Luc Illusie, Grothendieck and vanishing cycles, Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse 30 (2021), §1.1, formula (1.2), and §1.2, last paragraph, printed pp. 85–86: for a henselian trait S, X of finite type over S and K in D^b_c(X_eta), RPsi_f(K) = i~^* R jbar_*(K|X_etabar) lies in D^b_c(X_s~) (Deligne). Specialized to S strictly henselian (S~ = S, s~ = s), X separated, and K a constructible sheaf in degree zero; finite constant coefficient-ring form by retaining its action. Read online; local archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Write $f:X\to S$ and $j:X_\eta\hookrightarrow X$. Let $t$ generate the maximal ideal of $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] every nonzero $r\in R$ is $ut^n$ with $u$ a unit and $n\geq0$. Hence $R[1/t]=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, so $j$ is the open immersion $D(t)$; and every nonzero ideal is $t^nR$ for the least such exponent $n$ among its elements, so $R$ is a local principal ideal domain of dimension one, the form of the hypothesis in the two trait nodes used in Steps 3 and 7. The affine scheme $S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and is locally Noetherian because $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is Noetherian. On affine charts of $f$, the finite-type algebra over a Noetherian coordinate ring is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation; finite type supplies quasi-compactness; its diagonal is a closed immersion, so its inverse image over an affine open is affine and quasi-compact by the affine-scheme node, giving quasi-separatedness, so it is of finite presentation as defined in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Algebra 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) for the unit-times-power form; 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); finite-type Noetherian finite-presentation lemma; 01TP (definition-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Set $L=j_!F$ using [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Restriction to the open $X_\eta$ is $F$ directly from the defining presheaf and sheafification on that open. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], its restriction to the closed complement is zero: every geometric stalk there is zero, and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] detects this. Take the finite constructible stratification trivializing $F$ and append $X_k$ as a stratum with value zero. These remain locally closed constructible strata in the Noetherian scheme $X$, and show that $L$ is constructible by [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. We use this sheaf in degree zero; no resolution by finite free $\Lambda$-modules or finite Tor hypothesis is involved.

Put $m=\ell^n$. The ring $\Lambda$ is a $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-algebra because $m\Lambda=0$, and $m$ is invertible on $S$ because $\ell$ is. Apply [lem-trf-trait-nearby-base-change] to $f$ and to the bounded total-scheme complex $L$. Its conclusion is precisely that $(f,L)$ is $\Psi$-good. This step supplies a hypothesis of the next theorem, rather than assuming nearby-cycle constructibility.

Apply [lem-trf-psi-good-oriented-cohomology-strata] to $f$ and $L$: Step 1 gives the Noetherian base and finite presentation, Step 2 gives constructibility of $L$, and Step 3 gives $\Psi$-goodness and the coefficient condition. For each $q\geq0$ obtain partitions $X=\coprod X_\alpha$, $S=\coprod S_\beta$ on which the oriented cohomology sheaf $G_q=\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_fL)$ is finite locally constant. This theorem asserts cohomological constructibility only. We obtain the independent uniform vanishing bound in Steps 9–10.

source.place: Theorem 4.27(2), followed by the explicit finite-partition definition, printed pp. 36–37

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $k^a$ of $k$ and the corresponding closed geometric point $b$ of $S$. Here $S_{(b)}=S$. To verify this identification, take a pointed affine etale neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$. Its chosen residue-field extension of $k$ is separable algebraic by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable], hence equals $k$ since $k$ is separably closed. The resulting map $A\to k$ lifts uniquely to $A\to R$ by [lem-sc-etale-henselian-ring-lift], with target henselian local $R$, identity base map, and quotient $R\to k$. These unique sections are pointed and compatible with all neighbourhood maps. Consequently the identity pointed neighbourhood is initial, and the inverse limit defining $S_{(b)}$ in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] is $S$.

Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $K^s$ be the chosen separable closure, and choose an algebraic closure $K^a$ containing $K^s$. The extensions $k^a/k$ and $K^a/K^s$ are purely inseparable: an algebraic element over a separably closed field has a purely inseparable minimal polynomial. Their maps of spectra are integral (all elements are algebraic), surjective (one point), and radicial (the residue extensions are purely inseparable). By [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism] they are universal homeomorphisms, as are their base changes $a:X_{k^a}\to X_k$ and $h:X_{K^a}\to X_{K^s}$. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], their etale inverse images are equivalences preserving and reflecting covers. These equivalences extend to constant-$\Lambda$ modules by transporting the module operations, and termwise to derived categories; they are exact and preserve constant finite module sheaves.

Put $C=i^*R\bar j_*\pi^*F$ on $X_k$, and let $j_a:X_{K^a}\to X$. Apply [lem-trf-nearby-geometric-slice] to the total-scheme sheaf $L$, the closed geometric point $b$, and the generic point $\operatorname{Spec}K^a$ with the compatible specialization. Step 5 identifies its strict base with $S$. Its conclusion is $e_f^*R\Psi_fL\simeq (i a)^*Rj_{a*}(L|_{X_{K^a}})$. This is $a^*C$: indeed $j_a=\bar j h$, $L|_{X_{K^a}}=h^*\pi^*F$, and the exact equivalence of Step 6 gives $Rh_*h^*=1$. At the derived-functor level the composition here is valid because the right adjoint $h_*$ of an exact equivalence preserves injectives; applying direct images to an injective resolution gives $Rj_{a*}=R\bar j_*Rh_*$. Thus we have $a^*C\simeq e_f^*R\Psi_fL$, with the same finite ring throughout.

source.place: (1.3.4) and its geometric-slice identification; 04DZ for the purely inseparable comparison

proof.text: Fix $q$. Refine the base partition of Step 4 by the two subsets $\{s\}$ and $\{\eta\}$ of the trait, and put $Z_\alpha=X_\alpha\times_S k$. The morphism $e_f$ of Step 7 on $Z_\alpha\times_k k^a$ factors through the oriented subtopos for $X_\alpha$ and the base stratum containing $\eta$: its two projections are the inclusion in $X_\alpha$ and the fixed generic geometric point, with the chosen specialization. This factorization is the universal property of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Inverse image pulls each local trivialization of $G_q$ back to a cover with the same finite constant values; hence $\mathcal H^q(a^*C)$ is finite locally constant on each $Z_\alpha\times_k k^a$. Inverse image on constant-module topoi is exact as specified in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. The cover-preserving equivalence of [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], also on each $Z_\alpha$, descends these local trivializations to $Z_\alpha$. The finitely many $Z_\alpha$ partition $X_k$ into constructible locally closed strata. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], $\mathcal H^q(C)$ is constructible.

source.place: Finite-partition definition after Theorem 4.27; restriction along the slice of Illusie (1.3.4); 04DZ for descent of trivializing covers

proof.text: Since $f$ is finite type and $S$ is quasi-compact, [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] gives $d\geq0$ bounding the dimensions of all fibres of $f$. Apply [lem-trf-gabber-strict-local-torsion-bound] with $m=\ell^n$, coefficient ring $\Lambda$, $N=d$, and, for each geometric point $x$ of $X$, the sheaf $L|_{X_{(x)}}$. This gives $R^qf_{(x)*}(L|_{X_{(x)}})=0$ for every $q>2d$, uniformly in $x$. It requires neither constructibility nor finite Tor dimension of this sheaf.

For each geometric point $x$, [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-strict-local-description] identifies $\sigma_x^*R\Psi_fL$ with $Rf_{(x)*}(L|_{X_{(x)}})$; $\sigma_x^*$ is exact. Step 9 therefore shows $\sigma_x^*G_q=0$ for $q>2d$. The same cited statement says that the family $\sigma_x^*$ is jointly conservative, so $G_q=0$ on $V_f$ for $q>2d$. Its inverse image in Step 7 is zero as well. Exactness and conservativity of the equivalence $a^*$ from Step 6 give $\mathcal H^q(C)=0$ for $q>2d$. This proves a single global bound, rather than bounds depending on a special-fibre stalk.

source.place: (1.12.6) and Corollary 1.15; joint conservativity of the strict-local sections

proof.text: Finally [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes $i^*$ exact on constant-$\Lambda$ modules. An exact additive functor preserves kernels and images, so it commutes with cohomology of a representative complex. The definition of higher direct image in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] consequently gives $\mathcal H^q(C)=i^*R^q\bar j_*(\pi^*F)$. Steps 8 and 10 establish respectively its constructibility for every $q\geq0$ and its vanishing for $q>2d$.

source.place: 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), and the definition of higher direct image

proof_origin.place: Combination of Theorem 4.27(2) and Example 4.26(2) with Illusie Around Thom–Sebastiani (1.3.4), (1.12.6), Corollary 1.15, and explicit extension-by-zero and inseparable-closure comparisons. Primary PDFs read online; archival copies WANTED. The original Illusie 2021 summary is not used as a stronger finiteness input.

Theorem 4.27(2): if S has finitely many irreducible components, f is of finite presentation, Λ is Noetherian and m-torsion, L is in D_c and (f,L) is Ψ-good, then RΨ_f L is in D_c; constructible means finitely generated stalks and finite partitions of X and S into constructible locally closed subsets, with each restriction to an oriented product locally constant. It does not restate its parent. Steps 1–11 are correct. Step 1 gives finite presentation. Step 2 shows j_!F is constructible. Step 3 gets Ψ-goodness from the trait node. Step 5 shows S_(b)=S: the base is its own strict localization, because the identity neighbourhood is initial. Step 8 factors e_f through the oriented product containing η and descends local constancy. Steps 9–10 prove one uniform vanishing bound q>2d through Gabber's bound and joint conservativity. Step 11 uses exactness of i^*. No excellence, finite Tor or SGA source is used. Every dependency's unit is on the sk-i-curve-zero route, and there is no cycle.
